title: The opener and memory consolidation start without a machine slot; run_tests.py outside a slot never waits for one (issue #7)
objective: An opener never waits for a machine slot, while a test run it starts still takes a slot (without waiting) or reports the machine busy.
outline: devloop/core/agents.py: a module constant naming the roles that take no slot (for example NO_SLOT_ROLES = ("creator", "consolidator", "consolidator_peer")). Pending.launch() skips, for self.role in it, both the 'slot' live record and slots.take(): self.slot stays None, waited stays 0, _spawn_next adds no DEVLOOP_SLOT (a nested opener still inherits its parent's DEVLOOP_SLOT through cfg.env, as today), release_when_done is not called. Every start goes through launch() (the first one, the quota fallback in _finish, the relaunch after _wait_for_quota), so this one check covers them. Update the module and launch() docstrings. devloop/run_tests.py: after Config(), when slots.needed(cfg): slot = slots.take(cfg, time.time()) (a deadline of now is exactly one try, gate included); None -> print the busy line to stderr and return 2 before making the output folder; otherwise os.environ[slots.ENV] = slot.path before testrun.run (cfg.env copies os.environ into the test interface's environment) and slot.release() in a finally. Add the busy case to the module docstring. devloop/prompts/creator/01-role.md: one short paragraph after 'You read the code to understand what exists; you do not change the code.' (not 02-rules.md or 03-handin.md: the issue #6 tickets rewrite their DAG parts). memory/role/creator.md: that one line only. devloop/README.md '## Machine slots': the 'What takes a slot' sentence and a sentence on run_tests.py.

notes: Issue #7 (GitHub sai99claw/agent-control #7). User (T, verbatim): 「開題者 理論上不用等 regression， 驗證在跑的時候只會阻擋後續的票繼續進行開發寫code， 不會阻擋新的票題設計」. Today Pending.launch() takes a slot (slots.take(cfg, None), no time limit) for every role, so with devloop.regression_exclusive the opener waits for the whole regression (T, 2026-11-23: three openers waited 2+ hours, one carrying a prod fix). Design decisions by the opener: (1) the role check sits in launch() because every start of a run passes there; (2) run_tests.py does not wait: one try, then run or exit 2, so no wait is charged to any time limit and a stop leaves nothing held (the flock goes with the process); (3) DEVLOOP_SLOT is exported to the test run it starts, because anything devloop-started inside a slot holder must take none or it deadlocks at machine_slots 1 (project memory: nested runs); the loop test base already strips DEVLOOP_SLOT for its own loops; (4) the prompt text goes in 01-role.md and names $AC_HOME (set by cfg.env for every agent) because the chain has no placeholders and the project root is not always agent-control. A run_tests.py that holds a slot delays a waiting exclusive regression by that test run, like any slot holder. MachineSlots.test_an_agent_has_no_no_slot_state_and_counts_its_wait asserts the double-quoted text "no slot" never appears in devloop/core/agents.py, and MachineSlots.test_the_slot_section_has_no_no_slot_outcome_and_says_the_clocks_start_at_the_slot asserts it is not in the README slot section: do not write it there with double quotes. hard_block patterns match every added line of the branch, tests and comments included: never write os.kill, killpg, pkill or 'kill -' anywhere (use a Popen object's own methods). docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/VISION.md are the main session's (hard_block paths): do not edit them. No absolute home paths in any file (tests/test_no_project_names.py scans every tracked file, .md included). CODE-MAP.md is regenerated at landing: do not edit it. Test ids given to run_tests.py are module ids relative to the unittest roots (test_machine.Class), never tests_devloop.test_machine.Class.
acceptance: Roles creator (opener and reviser), consolidator and consolidator_peer start their command without taking a machine slot: with devloop.machine_slots 1 and <worktrees>/slots/slot-0 held (flock LOCK_EX) by another holder that releases it only after 20 s, `python3 devloop/ticket_creator.py --request x` (fake creator, default hand-in) exits 0 in under 15 s, before the slot is released.

With devloop.machine_slots 2, devloop.regression_exclusive true and a LOCK_EX held on <worktrees>/slots/exclusive that is released only after 20 s, `python3 devloop/ticket_creator.py --request x` exits 0 in under 15 s, before the mark is released.

In process, with devloop.machine_slots 1 and slot-0 held by the test (released by a timer after 8 s), agents.run(cfg, role, 'go', <project>, <run dir>, 30) returns in under 4 s with hand.problem() None and an empty DEVLOOP_SLOT seen by the command, for each of the roles creator, consolidator and consolidator_peer; the command is the one test_machine.py MachineSlots.test_an_agent_slot_is_free_when_it_exits_though_its_background_child_lives uses, without its `sleep 20 &` (it writes {"kind": "done", "slot": "$DEVLOOP_SLOT"} to $DEVLOOP_RESULT), so hand.result['slot'] == ''.

The live record of such an agent never has state 'slot': with core.inflight.put patched to collect each record's 'state', the agents.run of the previous item for role creator collects only 'running' (one or more times) and never 'slot'.

Roles worker (also run with chain_role worker_simple), verifier, reviewer and fixer take a slot exactly as today: they wait for a held slot and for a held exclusive mark (the existing T30Acceptance and MachineSlots cases keep passing unchanged).

`python3 devloop/run_tests.py <ids>` in a process with DEVLOOP_SLOT unset and devloop.machine_slots set tries once to take a slot, without waiting and honouring the exclusive mark (slots.take(cfg, time.time())); when it gets none (every slot held, or regression_exclusive true and slots/exclusive held LOCK_EX by another process) it runs nothing, writes exactly one line to stderr, `run_tests: machine busy (a regression holds the machine or every machine slot is taken); nothing was run`, writes nothing to stdout, and exits 2, all in under 5 s; the test interface is not started (the $FAKE_INTERVALS file stays absent or empty).

When it gets a slot, run_tests.py runs the ids as today (same exit codes: 0 green, 1 red, 86 environment, 2 could not measure), the test command runs with DEVLOOP_SLOT set to that slot's file (<worktrees>/slots/slot-0 with machine_slots 1, so anything devloop-started inside it takes no slot of its own), and the slot is free again once run_tests.py has exited.

With DEVLOOP_SLOT set (run under an agent's slot) or with devloop.machine_slots null, run_tests.py takes no slot and never says machine busy, even with every slot and the exclusive mark held (as today).

The opener's prompt chain (ticket_creator.chain(); the text goes in devloop/prompts/creator/01-role.md) says to run tests only through `python3 "$AC_HOME/devloop/run_tests.py" <test ids>` (from the tree to be tested), and that when it prints machine busy the opener neither waits nor runs it again but writes the ticket with that premise marked `not measured (machine busy)`: chain() contains `run_tests.py`, `machine busy` and `not measured (machine busy)`.

devloop/README.md section '## Machine slots' says that the opener (role creator, also when revising) and memory consolidation (consolidator, consolidator_peer) take no slot and start at once even while a regression holds the machine, and that run_tests.py outside a slot takes one without waiting or exits 2 with machine busy: the section contains `creator`, `consolidator_peer` and `machine busy`, still contains every phrase the existing README cases look for (agent, red check, regression, slots/slot-, own limit, DEVLOOP_SLOT, parent's slot, wait for a slot without a limit, from when the slot is taken, still counts against `regression_timeout_seconds`, regression_exclusive, slots/exclusive, needs `machine_slots`) and never contains the double-quoted text "no slot".

memory/role/creator.md's line that starts 'Reproduce the precondition yourself once' says how to run it: a throwaway test file under the test roots of a scratch worktree, run there with `python3 "$AC_HOME/devloop/run_tests.py" <test ids>`, and a premise that got machine busy is marked not measured (checked once in the hand-in; no permanent case, because the consolidator rewrites memory files).

Old cases changed in place: tests_devloop/test_machine.py T3Acceptance.test_an_agent_waits_for_the_slot_and_runs_once_it_is_freed and T4Acceptance.test_v2_a_held_mark_keeps_every_taker_waiting_until_it_is_released assert that the opener waits. They keep their fixture (slot-0, resp. slots/exclusive, held and released by a 3 s timer; agent_timeout_seconds 2) but run a worker in process (agents.run(cfg, 'worker', ...) with the worker command T30Acceptance.done_worker sets) and assert it started only after the release; their docstrings say the opener takes no slot since issue #7.

request:
# Two design changes reported by tabby_pool (T) as GitHub issues #7 and #6 on sai99claw/agent-control

The user approved both designs below (2026-11-23, "Ok" to the main session's proposal). Each ticket names its issue number so the main session can close the issue after landing. Issue texts are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file.

Order: #6's ticket(s) depend on every ticket opened from the request for issues #1 #2 #4 #5 (they are open in the pool now and change ticket_controller.py too) and on #7's ticket. #7's ticket depends on nothing open.

## Issue #7: the opener does not wait for a machine slot
User (T, verbatim): 「開題者 理論上不用等 regression， 驗證在跑的時候只會阻擋後續的票繼續進行開發寫code， 不會阻擋新的票題設計」.
Today devloop/core/agents.py `Pending.launch()` takes a machine slot (`slots.take`, no time limit) for every role. With `devloop.regression_exclusive: true` the regression holds the gate and every slot, so `actl new` waits for hours while a regression runs (T, 2026-11-23: three openers waited 2+ hours, one carrying a prod fix).
Wanted:
- The roles that only read the repo and write tickets or memory start without a slot: the opener / reviser (role creator) and the consolidator (and its peer). Worker, verifier, reviewer and fixer keep taking a slot. The live record of an opener never shows the "slot" stage.
- The opener sometimes runs tests to measure a premise (memory/role/creator.md "Verify the ticket's premises"). Those runs must not land inside an exclusive regression: devloop/run_tests.py, when its process is not under a slot (DEVLOOP_SLOT unset) and slots are needed, tries to take one without waiting; when none is free (or the exclusive gate is held) it prints one line saying the machine is busy (regression running or all slots taken) and exits 2 (could not measure) without running anything. Under a slot it behaves as today.
- The opener's prompt (devloop/prompts/creator/) says: run tests only through `python3 <loop>/run_tests.py <ids>`; on "machine busy" do not wait or retry, write the ticket with that premise marked "not measured (machine busy)". Update memory/role/creator.md's measuring line if it names another way to run tests.
- removes: the opener's unbounded wait for a slot.

## Issue #6: groups are chosen by the opener and form a chain; a group's regression is a dependency point
User (T, verbatim): 「Group 的數量定義 應該是開題者決定的 而不是固定10 開題者在寫入dag的時候 本來就會去看其他的題目是什麼然後要把自己的題放在哪裡， Group 的regression 就是一個強制產生相依性的地方， Dag 的尾巴一定是個group , 因為dag表示了現在所有要做的票，最後一個做完一定需要整個驗一次。 所以說開題者他要做的事情就是把他當前在開的題目找到一個合適的比較不容易產生衝突的或是邏輯相近的票的附近放進去」.
Today tickets fill the open group up to `max_group_size` (10) and then a new group opens; several groups run from different main shas and serialize only at the regression, so each landing makes a waiting group merge main and run its 1.2-hour regression again (T: g57 landing re-ran g56), and cross-group conflicts show up late in fix rounds.
Design the main session and the user agreed:
1. The opener assigns every new ticket to a group when it writes dag.json: an existing group that has not started its regression (state open: no member past merged and no regression started), or a new group at the end. It picks the group whose tickets are logically closest / least likely to conflict, and says why in the ticket's notes. Writing a ticket into a group that is already pr/fixing/verified/landed is refused by the pool write validation (the opener's one retry then picks another group).
2. Groups form one chain in creation order. A group's regression starts only when every earlier group is landed or cancelled. A later group's tickets may start work before that (worker, verifier, reviewer on the group's branch), as long as their own ticket dependencies allow; when the earlier group lands, the branch takes main as today (follow_main) and then its regression runs once.
3. A stuck earlier group holds the later groups' regressions; its page
